candidates.name: Ramekin-to-Plate Phase-Balanced X-VLA Adapter
candidates.core_idea: Use training-only HDF5 geometry to label source-on-ramekin, transit, and target-on-plate chunks, then give the underrepresented transit and placement phases explicit influence in a small adapter/OFT training objective while preserving the original deployment inputs.
candidates.why_this_matches_the_residual: All three policy references fail the exact bowl-on-ramekin to plate transfer, while the data audit shows balanced enough source/transit/target supervision and no overlap with the residual initial state. The candidate attacks the observed transition/placement bottleneck rather than reopening older broad verifier or repair families.

candidates.name: Clearance-Triggered Temporal Requery X-VLA
candidates.core_idea: Reduce action-chunk staleness around inferred lift-off and placement windows by forcing shorter temporal requery or lower-horizon chunk execution near the source-to-target handoff.
candidates.why_considered: The first prior took 30 chunks and failed, while OpenVLA-OFT needed 28 chunks and also failed; a temporal-wrapper hypothesis is a plausible lightweight explanation to rule out.
candidates.why_not_selected: The existing evidence does not show that the failure is primarily chunk staleness rather than object-contact, lift, or placement policy content. A requery wrapper risks becoming a heuristic control and may require privileged or brittle phase detection if not carefully constrained.
